summary: Repository authoring follows lane capability and approved scope. Non-editing lanes deny native shell and named editors. A closed capability ceiling authenticates the dispatched child and attempt before native or nested MCP execution, without overriding narrower host permissions. Non-editing checks select only recorded executable controls through the existing execution owner. Ordinary check strings grant no execution authority. Product-law approval, review, unmanaged host work, and the absence of a filesystem or network sandbox remain explicit boundaries.
title: Repository authoring follows lane capability and approved scope
